# `silk/allocator`

<!-- Generated by packages/compiler/scripts/generate-documentation.mjs. Do not edit by hand. -->

Foundational allocation service used by higher standard-library actors.

## When to use

Provide [`Allocator`](#declaration-73696c6b2f616c6c6f6361746f723a3a416c6c6f6361746f72) to operations that may create owned storage, normally with
[`SystemAllocator`](#declaration-73696c6b2f616c6c6f6361746f723a3a53797374656d416c6c6f6361746f72).

## Details

[`Allocator`](#declaration-73696c6b2f616c6c6f6361746f723a3a416c6c6f6361746f72) is an ordinary source-declared service. Its requirement remains in an Effect
until a caller supplies a provider, so tests and applications can replace the process-backed
implementation lexically. Allocation failure is typed as [`OutOfMemoryError`](#declaration-73696c6b2f616c6c6f6361746f723a3a4f75744f664d656d6f72794572726f72).

## Examples

### Provide the process allocator

```silk
import silk.allocator { Allocator }

import silk.bytes as Bytes

import silk.effect { Effect }

import silk.usize as usize

effect fn copyMessage() -> i32
! Allocator.OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorService()
  let source = b"Silk"
  let copying = Bytes.copy(&source)
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let bytes = run copying
  return Bytes.length(&bytes)
    |> usize.toI32
}

effect fn recoverAllocation(error: Allocator.OutOfMemoryError) -> i32 {
  return 0
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  return run Effect.catchAll(copyMessage(), recoverAllocation)
}
```

Import as `Allocator` with `import silk.allocator`.

## `outOfMemory`

```silk
pub effect fn outOfMemory() -> never ! OutOfMemoryError
```

Fails immediately with `OutOfMemoryError`.

### When to use

Use this function to translate a checked size failure into the standard allocation failure.

